description: Aura Phase-G = masterplan Phase 4 (collapse the agent runtime / kill legacy agent.Runner). Runner is the residual duplicate flagged in PRD §6 and docs/aura-main-loop-limits-audit.md §1. After Phase-F (Phase-3 streaming-protection arc) the canonical path is chat.Hub → chat.AgentLoop → agent.Run (loop.go). Runner is a stateful wrapper around that same agent.Run with mutable LimitController glue for the dashboard. 4 live consumers: cmd/aura/app.go (constructor + cron adapter), internal/api/web_chat.go, internal/telegram/deps.go, internal/cron/dispatch.go (via adapter). 7 stories: introduce stateless agent.RunTask, migrate each consumer one by one, simplify LimitController, then delete runner.go + runner_test.go and refresh docs. Full call graph + per-story scope in .planning/deep-refactor/Phase04_Collapse_Agent_Runtime/progress.md. Each story = ONE atomic commit on master.

userStories.title: Stateless agent.RunTask helper
userStories.description: Introduce a stateless agent.RunTask function that does what Runner.Run does today, so Phase-G consumers can migrate off the Runner struct without losing behavior. (a) internal/agent/runtask.go (new): func RunTask(ctx context.Context, deps RunTaskDeps, task Task) (Result, error) where RunTaskDeps groups the previously-Runner-held fields {LLM llm.Client; Tools *tools.Registry; Model string; ReasoningEffort string; PhantomGuard *PhantomToolGuard; Logger *slog.Logger} plus the previously-mutable limits {MaxIterations int; Timeout time.Duration; ToolTimeout time.Duration} (read once per call — runtime config changes apply to the NEXT call). (b) Body mirrors Runner.Run: context.WithTimeout wrap, initialMessages(task), cleanToolList, agentExecutor + NewNoStreamClient + Invocation, call internal/agent.Run, wrap rtResult into Result with the MaxIterationsHit fallback message. (c) Task, Result, RunTaskDeps stay in a new internal/agent/task.go file (extracted from runner.go in US-G06). For US-G01 we DEFINE these types as fresh aliases/copies so RunTask compiles standalone; the legacy Runner keeps using the same names from runner.go until US-G06. (d) initialMessages, cleanToolList, limitToolContent currently live in runner.go — copy them to a new internal/agent/runtask_helpers.go (private). They'll be deleted from runner.go in US-G06 when the wrapper goes. (e) Test internal/agent/runtask_test.go: ≥3 cases (happy path, MaxIterationsHit fallback message, prompt-or-messages-required error) using the same in-process LLM fake style as runner_test.go.
acceptanceCriteria: RunTask returns the same MaxIterationsHit fallback string as Runner.Run when rtResult.Stats.MaxIterationsHit is true
RunTask returns 'agent: prompt or messages required' when task has neither
Runner / runner.go / runner_test.go UNCHANGED in this story (migration starts in US-G02..G04)
Single atomic commit prefix: feat(agent): stateless RunTask helper (US-G01)
userStories.notes: RunTaskDeps is intentionally a wider struct than Runner.Config so callers don't need to construct an intermediate Runner. The fields the dashboard mutates at runtime (MaxIterations, Timeout, ToolTimeout) move from Runner.mu-guarded fields to per-call parameters — the caller reads cfg fresh.

userStories.title: Audit + drop telegram.Deps.agentRunner
userStories.description: internal/telegram/deps.go has `agentRunner *agent.Runner` on Deps + Bot. Audit every method on *telegram.Bot for actual callers. (a) Grep `b.deps.agentRunner`, `b.agentRunner`, `Bot.AgentRunner` across internal/telegram and channels/telegram. (b) If there are zero live callers, remove the field from `Deps` and the corresponding field on `Bot`; update cmd/aura/app.go to stop passing it in `telegram.Deps{...}` literals. (c) If there ARE callers (likely background ops / scheduler glue), migrate each to call agent.RunTask directly with the deps already held by the bot (b.LLMClient(), b.ToolRegistry(), b.cfg.LLMModel, b.cfg.ReasoningEffort, etc.). Each migrated call site reads RunTaskDeps fresh from the bot config so dashboard live-tune still works. (d) Tests: any test in internal/telegram that injects a Runner gets refactored to inject the same deps (or stubbed RunTaskDeps). No new test scaffolding — reuse what already exists.

userStories.title: Migrate internal/api/web_chat.go off agent.Runner
userStories.description: internal/api/web_chat.go holds `runner *agent.Runner` and calls `s.runner.Run(ctx, task)` per /api/chat request. (a) Replace the `runner` field with a `deps func() agent.RunTaskDeps` lazy-builder (or an explicit RunTaskDeps stored at construction time — pick the simplest of the two; lazy avoids stashing stale limits at startup). (b) `webChatService.Chat` builds RunTaskDeps + Task and calls `agent.RunTask(ctx, deps, task)`. (c) Update `NewWebChatService` signature: drop `runner *agent.Runner` parameter, accept the same fields RunTaskDeps wraps (LLM, tools, model, reasoningEffort, phantomGuard, logger, limits getter). (d) Chase the single call site in cmd/aura/app.go that calls `NewWebChatService(...)` and pass the new args from `deps` / `cfg`. (e) Tests in internal/api/ that exercise web_chat must still pass; if a test injects a Runner stub, replace it with a RunTaskDeps stub that returns a fake LLM.
acceptanceCriteria: NewWebChatService signature updated; the one cmd/aura/app.go call site is updated
Existing internal/api tests pass without modification of their assertions

userStories.title: Drop AgentLimitController runtime mutation
userStories.description: internal/config/runtime_settings.go::ApplyRuntimeSettings takes a `runner config.AgentLimitController` parameter and calls `runner.UpdateLimits(...)` to mutate the Runner's limits live. With the consumers migrated (US-G02..G04) and Runner about to be deleted (US-G06), this knob has nothing to mutate. (a) Drop the `runner config.AgentLimitController` parameter from ApplyRuntimeSettings. (b) Delete the config.AgentLimitController interface (declared in internal/config/) and any test fakes that satisfy it. (c) Update cmd/aura/app.go's single call site to pass one fewer arg. (d) cfg.AuraBotMaxIterations / AuraBotTimeoutSec STILL update from settings (that part is unchanged — they live on the Config struct). They just propagate to NEXT agent.RunTask invocation instead of mutating a live runner. (e) Confirm via test that dashboard settings still flow into Config; the change is only that there's no longer a runner instance to push limits into.
